title: Split-Head Quantum Generative Adversarial Network for Crystalline Material Discovery
authors: Huan-Ming Chang, Jen-Yu Chang, Tsung-Wei Huang, En-Jui Kuo
abstract: The discovery of novel crystalline materials is a critical challenge in computational materials science, often limited by the spatial representation limitations and mode collapse typical of classical generative models. Traditionally, developing Quantum GANs for continuous 3D space is hindered by the limited capacity of near-term hardware. To overcome this, we adapt a physics-informed "split-head" architecture right from the quantum trunk to explicitly decouple macroscopic lattice bounds from microscopic atomic coordinates, significantly maximizing resource efficiency. This study disentangles the contributions of quantum circuits from these architectural priors by evaluating a Split-Head Quantum Generative Adversarial Network against an architecture-matched classical ablation model. Evaluated on the highly constrained Mg-Mn-O system, the results reveal a highly nuanced performance dichotomy between the advanced models. The architecture-matched classical ablation model demonstrated superior thermodynamic precision. Conversely, the integration of quantum circuits in the SH-QGAN drove unparalleled structural breadth and latent space exploration, more than doubling the ablation's geometric validity and successfully generating novel, metastable candidates converging on the Mg2MnO4 stoichiometry. These findings clarify that while architectural separation of cell and atom generation drives strict thermodynamic precision, quantum feature mapping independently provides the spatial diversity necessary to overcome mode collapse. Both mechanisms offer distinct, complementary enhancements for the generative discovery of advanced materials.
summary: This paper introduces a Split-Head Quantum GAN (SH-QGAN) to accelerate the discovery of novel crystalline materials. By separating the prediction of global lattice parameters from local atomic coordinates, the model leverages quantum circuits to achieve unparalleled structural diversity while maintaining high thermodynamic precision. The results demonstrate that combining quantum feature mapping with physics-informed architectural priors is a powerful paradigm for generative materials science.
main_problem: Discovering novel, stable crystalline materials is limited by classical generative models' inability to explore vast 3D chemical space without mode collapse.
main_result: The SH-QGAN successfully generates structurally diverse candidates that exhibit superior thermodynamic stability and geometric validity compared to purely classical ablation models.
method: A physics-informed Split-Head Quantum GAN (SH-QGAN) is employed, which decouples lattice parameter prediction from atomic coordinate generation using quantum circuits for enhanced exploration.
model_or_system: The system studied is the Mg-Mn-O crystalline material space. The model uses an SH-QGAN architecture with a classical WGAN-GP discriminator to generate structures by predicting global cell parameters and local atomic coordinates separately.
key_observables: Thermodynamic stability (Energy Above Convex Hull, E_hull), Topological Validity Rate, Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and electronic bandgap (3.07 eV for the candidate).
important_parameters: The model is evaluated on a constrained core dataset of Mg-Mn-O structures; training involves specific learning rates and micro-batch sizes.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that decoupling lattice bounds from atomic coordinates (Split-Head) allows the quantum circuit to independently provide necessary spatial diversity beyond classical architectural constraints.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SH-QGAN schematic, loss convergence over epochs, structural hit-rate comparisons against ablation models, and electronic band structures confirming insulating properties for generated candidates.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of generative materials discovery, details the SH-QGAN architecture (decoupling heads), presents training methodologies using WGAN-GP, evaluates performance by comparing it to a classical ablation model, and concludes with DFT validation of top candidates.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter structure generation, the core methodology—using quantum circuits to enhance generative sampling in high-dimensional physical spaces—is highly relevant for developing ML models that respect underlying physical symmetries and constraints.

The diagram illustrates the data re-uploading sequence of the latent vector z, the internal topology of the parameterized quantum circuit (highlighting rotation gates and entanglement layers), and the physical bifurcation of the resultant expectation values into the independent Cell and Atom decoding heads before final Wasserstein evaluation.

Fig. 2. Thermodynamic evaluation of generative models. Top (Figure 2.a): Ternary phase diagram of the Mg-Mn-O composition space. The background color gradient indicates absolute Formation Energy (Ef) in eV/atom. White dots denote stable baseline phases defining the true Convex Hull. Red, purple, and green dots represent structures generated by the QGAN-v4, Classical Ablation, and Classical CNN, respectively. Bottom (Figure 2.b): Energy Above Convex Hull (Ehull) stability distribution. The solid red line designates perfect stability (Ehull = 0), while the boundaries at 0.08 eV/atom and 0.12 eV/atom denote the metastable threshold and observation limit.
